children: Stock index futures were higher on Friday while Treasury yields fell as investors focused on talks around reopening the Strait of Hormuz.
Here are the five news items investors should watch:
Burry flags AI capital spending:
Michael Burry warned that aggressive AI infrastructure investment by Microsoft
, Amazon
, Alphabet (GOOG, GOOGL), Meta Platforms
, and Oracle
could

result in significant write-offs. He said S&P 500 net capital investment reached 2.07% of GDP as of June 30, a level exceeded only once in nearly four decades, in the period following the March 2000 Nasdaq peak.
Musk expands xAI computing capacity:
Elon Musk said xAI's Colossus 2 could more than double its current Nvidia
chip count by year-end as the company expands its Memphis-area AI cluster. The
currently has 110,000 GB200s and 440,000 GB300s, with another 220,000 GB300s expected next week and a further 220,000 in November, underscoring continued demand for Nvidia's AI accelerators.
Goldman underweights AI borrowers
: Goldman Sachs Asset Management is underweight the largest AI borrowers as it expects a wave of additional hyperscaler debt issuance, Lindsay Rosner,
of multi-sector fixed-income investing, said in a Bloomberg TV interview. Amazon
, Meta Platforms
, and Alphabet (GOOG, GOOGL) have been among the biggest high-grade corporate bond issuers this year as Big Tech funds AI infrastructure projects.
China EV exports jump 33%:

China's global electric-vehicle exports rose 33% year over year to 284,622 units in August, according to Bloomberg, citing China Customs data. Year-to-date shipments reached 2.11 million, up 53%, with Belgium the largest destination, followed by Australia, Brazil, Thailand, and the UK, adding to competitive pressure for automakers in overseas markets.
EU weighs UK trade alignment:

The European Union has told Britain that higher tariffs on Chinese vehicles and closer alignment with EU trade policy could help avoid barriers under proposed “Made in Europe” rules, the Financial Times reported. The issue could affect Britain's auto industry, while Prime Minister Andy Burnham has pushed for the UK to receive “trusted partner” status under the bloc's planned framework.
